name: Ultrasound-assisted liposuction (VASER)

lead: Ultrasound-assisted liposuction (UAL) uses ultrasonic energy to emulsify fat before it is removed through thin cannulas. The third-generation system sold as VASER pulses the energy through a specialized probe. Surgeons use it to sculpt the abdomen, flanks, back and chest, and for abdominal etching, which defines the lines of the abs for a more muscular-looking midsection.

Its use for appearance centres on body contour: removing fat over the muscle outline, and treating gynecomastia in men. Research includes randomized trials comparing UAL with surgical lipectomy or other devices, plus reviews comparing it with standard suction-assisted liposuction.

paras: The procedure is performed by a surgeon, usually under local or general anaesthesia, after tumescent fluid is infiltrated. Ultrasound is applied to loosen fat, which is then suctioned. Patients typically wear compression garments afterwards and recovery lasts days to weeks.

Risks are those of liposuction generally, including embolism, organ perforation, infection, seroma, skin necrosis, fluid imbalance and lidocaine toxicity, with deaths reported at about one per ten thousand cases as of 2011. Burns can occur if the ultrasound probe becomes hot, and earlier devices were linked to tissue damage from excess ultrasound exposure.

chain: Ultrasound loosens fat in targeted areas
Fat is suctioned from over the abdominal muscle outline
Visible ab lines and a slimmer waist
angle.text: Surgeons remove fat selectively, including along the lines of the abdominal wall, so the underlying muscle shape shows more clearly. People use it as a finishing procedure for an already lean physique and to treat gynecomastia.

lead: Ultrasound-assisted liposuction is a body-contouring surgery in which ultrasonic energy liquefies fat so it can be suctioned from under the skin. The third-generation VASER system delivers pulsed energy through a specialized probe, and people choose it to refine the shape of the abdomen, flanks and chest. [1][2]

A common appearance use is abdominal etching, first described in 1993 as part of high-definition liposculpture, which accentuates the contours of the linea alba and the tendinous intersections of the rectus abdominis so a lean abdomen looks more defined. [3]

Published work includes randomized trials comparing ultrasonic liposuction with surgical lipectomy and with other ultrasound devices, and reviews comparing UAL with standard suction-assisted and laser-assisted liposuction. [4][5][6]

paras: UAL is one of several liposuction techniques grouped by the energy used to liquefy fat. [3] A review of the third-generation vibration amplification of sound energy at resonance (VASER) device describes it as suited to more superficial and fibrous fat. [1]

Third-generation devices use pulsed energy and a specialized probe to address the tissue damage associated with UAL devices used in the 1980s and 1990s, which was attributed to excessive ultrasound exposure. [2]

Surgeons use UAL for hard-to-treat areas, for gynecomastia, and for secondary liposuction. [2] Abdominal etching, a form of high-definition liposculpture, aims to show the contours of the abdominal wall. [3]
A classification paper on gynecomastia described a role for UAL in treating male breast enlargement, which affects 32 to 65 percent of men. [7]

Burns can occur if the ultrasound probe becomes hot. General liposuction risks include embolism, organ perforation, infection, seroma, skin necrosis, fluid imbalance and lidocaine toxicity; as of 2011, deaths were reported at about one per ten thousand cases. [2]
A randomized trial of 40 patients compared abdominal ultrasonic liposuction with surgical lipectomy. [4]
A 2024 randomized intraindividual study compared two ultrasound-assisted devices on the abdomen. [8]
A 2018 review of 25 articles comparing suction-assisted liposuction with ultrasound- and laser-assisted liposuction looked for objective differences between techniques. [5]

A 2000 trial tested external ultrasound before tumescent liposuction against placebo ultrasound; a 2023 study looked at the short-term effect of VASER liposuction on lipid profile; and 2023 consensus recommendations addressed VASER use. [9][10][11]

timeline.event: Earlier ultrasound liposuction devices are associated with tissue damage. [2]
